title: Prescription Insurance on File Brand, Specialty Network and Injury-Drug Billing Settings
content:
Four class-level settings of **Prescription Insurance on File** decide what happens when a brand is dispensed although a generic is available, whether Kestrel's specialty pharmacy may bill the plan, and whether billing is limited to drugs for an accepted injury.

| Plan class | Patient pays brand-generic difference on a brand requested by the patient | Brand needs prior authorization when a generic is available | Kestrel's specialty pharmacy in the plan's specialty network | Only drugs for the accepted injury are billable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | No | No | Yes | No |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | No | No | Yes | No |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | No | No | Yes | No |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | Yes | No | Yes | No |
| Commercial Copay Plan | Yes | No | No | No |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Settings explained

- **Brand-generic difference** — whether the patient pays the brand-generic cost difference when a brand is dispensed at patient request.
- **Brand needs prior authorization** — whether a brand with an available generic needs prior authorization.
- **Specialty network** — whether Kestrel's specialty pharmacy is in the plan's specialty network.
- **Injury drugs only** — whether only drugs for the accepted injury are billable.

## Observations

- The two commercial classes charge the brand-generic difference; the Medicaid and workers' compensation classes instead require prior authorization for such a brand.
- The Commercial Copay Plan is the only class whose specialty network does not include Kestrel's specialty pharmacy.
- Billing limited to the accepted injury applies only under the Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit.
